Verified current snapshot: 2026-11-08. Public specification and component-specific implementation status. Internal tests are not an audit.

# SAAX current status

Last verified: 2026-11-06

## SAAX Protocol — Public Beta

SAAX Protocol is currently in public Beta. Immediate-payment functionality is available on Base mainnet, while escrow custody remains limited to testnet.

Independent external security review is pending. Although internal verification and reliability testing have been performed, these do not replace an independent security assessment.

Live transactions involve financial and technical risks, including potential loss of funds and irreversible blockchain transfers. Users should evaluate these risks carefully and use the platform at their own discretion.

This notice does not constitute a guarantee of reimbursement, dispute recovery, or financial protection.

SAAX is a commitment layer for autonomous commerce. The public discovery and commitment-creation interfaces are deployed. A separate operator-run integration has completed real Base Sepolia funding, release and refund with complete independent export verification for its defined test profile. These are different deployment scopes. Neither makes mainnet escrow available.

## Maturity at a glance

| Component | Status | Demonstrated scope |
| Protocol specification | Public specification — versioned | Protocol v1.0.3; Discovery profile 1.0.0 and acceptance-v1 are separate formats. Publication is not standards-body adoption. |
| Routing and immediate payments | Public beta | Existing x402 USDC payments on Base mainnet 8453; direct payments, no mainnet custody. |
| Signed discovery, preflight and buyer acceptance | Beta | Public signed profile, free nonbinding preflight, configured-buyer acceptance creating one authenticated commitment. No payment or service execution is triggered. |
| Verification and receipts | Beta | Actual JWS crypto for Discovery records; verification is format-specific. General COSE/JWS evidence hooks remain distinct. GET /receipt?txHash=... resolves a settled transaction hash to its commitment; verified live on 2026-11-06. |
| Custody / financial integration | Testnet preview — not approved for mainnet funds | Separately signed Base Sepolia profile, authenticated agreement/evaluator, actual test-USDC funding and signed release/refund, portable exports and public-chain verification. Financial execution is operator-run, not a public API. |
| Unreleased custody and governance candidates | Under development / security review | Custody V3 has an owner-approved snapshot for independent review; that review has not been completed. It is not an audit, not production readiness, and not deployment approval. Local candidate tests do not identify the deployed V1 contract. No completed independent audit or approved mainnet custody release. |
| Durable idempotency and reconciliation | Beta (deployed) | Durable payment idempotency (file-backed locally; Supabase/PostgreSQL in the production topology), reconcile-before-respond, and a Supabase reconciliation RPC for stale pending operations. Verified by reliability and fault-injection suites; production multi-instance financial concurrency not yet exercised. |
| Financial-limit infrastructure (pilot) | Implemented / disabled | Per-buyer and global transaction limits, wallet allowlist, and atomic reservation engine are deployed with enforcement OFF. Pilot allowlist is not populated; no limits are active. Activation requires separate owner authorization. |

## Publicly deployed today

- GET /.well-known/saax.json: signed provider profile with explicit supported combinations. The preserved live profile identifies Base mainnet 8453.

- POST /prepare-commitment and MCP prepare_commitment: free compatibility checking and a provider-signed proposal. No agreement, funds, reserved capacity, service execution or spending authority.

- POST /accept-commitment and MCP accept_commitment: verifies an onboarded buyer's signed acceptance and records exactly one authenticated commitment. Durable proposal/acceptance storage supports retries; a new idempotency key does not make a single-use proposal reusable.

- Existing MCP tools and mainnet routing/immediate-payment services. A read-only release check performs MCP initialization, tool discovery, ping and protocol-info calls; an HTTP 200 alone is not treated as MCP proof.

The provider signature proves consistency with a key. Clients independently authenticate the provider key before installing it; configured-key trust is not permissionless publisher authentication. Buyer acceptance requires separately onboarded buyer keys. A key copied from an untrusted profile/export does not establish identity. See quickstart and trust onboarding (/docs#discovery-quickstart).

## Real Base Sepolia evidence

The latest financial closeout uses a separately signed testnet profile, exact eip155:84532 network and test-USDC CAIP-19 asset, six decimals, explicit escrow mode, and buyer-authorized seller/evaluator/custody/recovery terms. It rejects network or asset substitution; an RPC chain guard cannot rewrite signed terms.

Two minimal records each funded 1000 raw test-USDC units (0.001 test USDC):

- Successful release, block 55360516.

- Successful evaluator-signed refund, block 55360737.

The separate-process verifier ran without application database credentials: release78/78 and refund79/79 checks passed. It authenticates the profile/provider/buyer/complete terms/commitment/evaluator, verifies the deployed EIP-712 verdict at the execution block's timestamp, decodes the actual successful transactions/events, and checks historical custody/token outcomes. It also verifies signed fulfillment evidence and an evaluator signature connecting evidence to the verdict. These are internal software checks, not an independent security audit.

The fulfilled service is a deterministic local SHA-256 computation; the refund record is an authenticated test nonfulfillment declaration. Provider, buyer, seller and evaluator are operator-controlled test roles. No external customer, independent evaluator or public financial endpoint is claimed. Read the implementation walkthrough (/blog/signed-discovery-to-testnet-finance).

## Contract identity and historical corrections

The deployed testnet contract is CustodyV1 at 0x5a5472d751839cd4968cbf1b136baf862279ff5d, not the unreleased CustodyV3 candidate. Its runtime is 6934 bytes:6881 executable +51 CBOR metadata +2 length bytes. Pinned solc 0.8.26 compilation of the exact Git source matches the committed artifact and actual deployed runtime in full. Earlier metadata-length arithmetic was wrong; no new deployment was required. A code match establishes identity, not safety.

Earlier financial exports are retained as historical evidence. Their proposal terms did identify Sepolia, but they lacked the separately signed profile and complete buyer-authorized evaluator/evidence chain required by the stronger verifier. Their old39-check result is not complete end-to-end assurance. They are not rewritten or promoted by adding declarations.

## Recovery and custody limits

Discovery issuance recovery has been tested with replacement processes after durable acceptance and after issuance, preserving the same commitment. Specific financial crash/broadcast reconciliation scenarios have separate script evidence. These demonstrations do not prove every crash boundary, distributed failure, external-provider recovery or unattended operational service.

CustodyV1 can release under the agreed evaluator signature, refund under an evaluator-signed refund, or permit an unsigned timeout refund after the deadline while still Funded. A timeout refund is not an evaluator verdict. Disputed funds can remain frozen indefinitely if the evaluator disappears. There is no admin withdrawal, pause, upgrade or evaluator-replacement mechanism. Refunds and safety are not guaranteed.

## What remains before production custody

Mainnet custody deployment and spending are not enabled. Production signer/governance provisioning, exposure limits, operational recovery/canary parameters, legal review, target-chain release validation, independent security review and remediation remain open. Local candidate tests, a local chain configured as84532 and local EAS anchors are not proof of public Base Sepolia execution or public-chain finality. The new financial self-test does not claim an EAS anchor or L1-finality proof.

An external-participant pilot package exists but has not been sent; no external pilot completion or independent adoption is established. The Custody V3 snapshot is owner-approved as the baseline for independent review only; independent review has not been completed, and approval-for-review is not an audit, production readiness, or deployment approval.

## Documents

- Integration guide

- Versioned specification

- Verification walkthrough

- Security and risk boundaries

- Terms of use

SAAX remains experimental software with component-specific maturity labels. Mainnet immediate payments process real funds. Nothing here guarantees recovery, safety, audit status, legal compliance or financial outcomes.

# SAAX integration guide

## SAAX Protocol — Public Beta

SAAX Protocol is currently in public Beta. Immediate-payment functionality is available on Base mainnet, while escrow custody remains limited to testnet.

Independent external security review is pending. Although internal verification and reliability testing have been performed, these do not replace an independent security assessment.

Live transactions involve financial and technical risks, including potential loss of funds and irreversible blockchain transfers. Users should evaluate these risks carefully and use the platform at their own discretion.

This notice does not constitute a guarantee of reimbursement, dispute recovery, or financial protection.

Last verified: 2026-11-06

Start with the interface you intend to use. Public signed Discovery and buyer-authorized commitment creation do not move funds. Existing immediate payments are public beta on Base mainnet. The connected custody integration is a separate Base Sepolia testnet preview, operated through controlled scripts rather than public financial execution endpoints.

Read the terms (/terms) and current status (/status). No refund, safety, service-quality or independent-audit guarantee applies.

## Choose a supported path

| Path | Availability | What it does |
| Signed profile → preflight → buyer acceptance | Beta; publicly deployed | Creates a verifiable commitment after configured buyer authorization; no financial side effect. |
| Immediate x402 payment | Public beta; Base mainnet 8453 | Existing direct USDC payment flow, no mainnet escrow. |
| Discovery → custody → signed release/refund | Testnet preview; operator-run | Actual Base Sepolia 84532 test-USDC execution with complete independent export verification for the defined self-test. No public financial API. |
| Unreleased custody/governance candidates | Under development / security review | Not the deployed CustodyV1 implementation; Custody V3 has an owner-approved snapshot for independent review (review not completed &#8212; not an audit, not readiness, not deployment approval); no mainnet approval or completed independent audit. |

## Discovery quickstart

### 1. Authenticate the provider key independently

Download the public profile:

```
curl https://saax-protocol.com/.well-known/saax.json

```

The current provider is https://saax-protocol.com/, origin https://saax-protocol.com, keyId live-2026-11, Ed25519 JWK thumbprint KebjwLFLSV6LJFZ_Hp7ROBkVpHVBwrFNRgHkAQ5JldM. These are identifiers to compare, not an independent trust source merely because this page or the same server displays them. Confirm the provider/key mapping through a separately authenticated operator channel before installing it in your client's trust configuration. Verify the full profile signature, origin, version, active key validity and expiry against that configured key.

Supported trust is configured-key onboarding. DID, registry or automatically permissionless publisher authentication is not established. Signature validity and publisher identity are separate checks. Rotate a trust pin only after independently authenticating its replacement; preserve historical verification keys.

### 2. Request free, nonbinding preflight

Use an exact combination from the authenticated profile. The preserved public profile currently identifies eip155:8453 and Base-mainnet USDC. Do not execute that proposal on testnet. The operator-run financial preview uses a different, separately signed testnet profile.

Example request below is illustrative. Replace the buyer with your own address, generate a new nonce/time/deadline, and use the exact schema and combination in the verified live profile. Schema digests in that profile are provider declarations, not proof of an external schema audit.

```
{
"profileVersion": "1.0.0",
"capability": { "id": "security-scan" },
"schema": {
"id": "https://saax-protocol.com/schemas/commitment-manifest/v1",
"version": "1",
"digest": "sha256:3333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333"
},
"units": { "amount": "1000", "unit": "micro-units of settlement asset" },
"financialProfile": {
"network": "eip155:8453",
"asset": "eip155:8453/erc20:0x833589fcd6edb6e08f4c7c32d4f71b54bda02913",
"rail": "x402",
"mode": "x402"
},
"constraints": { "deadline": "REPLACE_WITH_FUTURE_UTC_ISO_TIME" },
"intendedParties": { "buyer": "REPLACE_WITH_YOUR_EVM_ADDRESS" },
"clientNonce": "REPLACE_WITH_UNIQUE_NONCE_AT_LEAST_8_CHARS",
"issuedAt": "REPLACE_WITH_CURRENT_UTC_ISO_TIME"
}

```

Save the completed request as prepare-request.json and send:

```
curl https://saax-protocol.com/prepare-commitment \
-H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
--data-binary @prepare-request.json

```

MCP prepare_commitment uses the same validation core. Verify the returned Ed25519 JWS over canonical proposal bytes, request digest, intended buyer/audience, schema/profile/manifest versions, network/asset/amount/decimals/unit, rail/mode, policy, nonce, issuedAt and expiry. Do not trust unsigned top-level copies instead of the signed representation.

Preflight charges no fee and creates no economic commitment, reservation, execution or spending authority. Identical nonce/request retries return the existing proposal; changed content under the same nonce conflicts. Proposals are offers-until-expiry subject to explicit stale-on-change revalidation, not guaranteed capacity.

### 3. Sign buyer acceptance, then create one commitment

A provider signature is not buyer consent. Acceptance requires a separately onboarded buyer Ed25519 public key mapped to the buyer identity and scope by the operator; possessing an arbitrary wallet address or copying a public key into the request does not register it. Unsupported buyers receive authorization errors. This is not permissionless buyer onboarding.

The acceptance-v1 document binds action accept_commitment, domain saax:acceptance:v1, intended provider/audience, buyer identity, proposalId and exact proposalDigest, termsDigest, profile/manifest/schema versions, an independent nonce, and a validity window. Sign canonical acceptance bytes with the registered buyer key. The operator revalidates supported terms, trust and expiry before durable acceptance.

```
{
"proposal": { "...": "FULL_SIGNED_PROPOSAL_UNCHANGED" },
"acceptance": { "...": "FULL_BUYER_SIGNED_ACCEPTANCE_V1" },
"idempotencyKey": "PERSIST_ONE_KEY_FOR_THIS_OPERATION"
}

```

Post this envelope to https://saax-protocol.com/accept-commitment, or call MCP accept_commitment. A successful first creation returns201; an identical retry returns the existing operation/commitment. Reusing a single-use proposal with a new key is rejected. The authenticated commitment contains manifest-v1 fields plus the real provider JWS wrapper manifest-v1.1+saax-proposal-bound; the historical COSE-shaped placeholder is not itself a cryptographic signature.

The operation may carry financial terms but creates no token approval, transfer, escrow funding, service execution or verdict. Later financial choices require their own signed terms and authorization. Do not equate proposalId, operationId, commitmentId, manifestHash, escrow ID or transaction hash.

## MCP integration

Endpoint:

```
https://www.saax-protocol.com/mcp

```

The release check initializes MCP and calls tools/list, ping and get_protocol_info. The deployed tool names are:

- get_protocol_info, get_routing_fee, ping

- route_request, list_capabilities

- get_commitment, list_commitments, get_commitment_status

- create_commitment

- get_evidence_verification, get_authority_validation

- prepare_commitment, accept_commitment

Client configuration varies by MCP client:

```
{ "mcpServers": { "saax": { "url": "https://www.saax-protocol.com/mcp" } } }

```

The older create_commitment tool is distinct from the new signed proposal/acceptance path. Its deterministic saax_... reference or a successful tool response does not establish the complete signed Discovery financial profile. Use the exact export verifier for the representation you received, not a generic claim that any commitment is fully verified.

## Existing immediate payments

The existing live mainnet Router uses x402 with Base USDC. The MPP rail implementation exists but is not registered in production (x402-only mode). The site HTTP route is https://saax-protocol.com/route; the settlement host https://settlement.saax-protocol.com is a separate existing integration surface. Read its current challenge before authorizing a payment. This website release does not change its payment code, fees, secrets or configuration.

A402 challenge supplies the amount, asset, network and payee. A separate wallet/payment authorization is required; Discovery acceptance does not pay. Confirm the actual successful settlement and its binding to your intended request. A transaction hash is not proof of success, fulfillment or refund rights. See what a receipt proves (/blog/x402-receipts-what-a-receipt-proves).

The x402 broadcaster may cover gas for its supported immediate-payment path; do not generalize this to custody transactions. Mainnet immediate payments are non-custodial and final, not escrow-backed.

## Testnet financial integration and independent verification

The isolated preview completes: separately signed testnet profile → provider proposal → buyer acceptance → commitment → real custody funding → signed evidence → evaluator-signed release or refund → complete export → independent verifier. It pins Base Sepolia 84532, USDC 0x036cbd53842c5426634e7929541ec2318f3dcf7e, six decimals and CustodyV1 0x5a5472d751839cd4968cbf1b136baf862279ff5d.

Network and CAIP-19 asset chain must agree across authenticated terms and execution. Mainnet terms cannot be interpreted as a testnet label, and no environment override changes the signed asset. Explicit mode:escrow differs from immediate-payment mode:x402; the preview's x402 compatibility rail label does not mean a facilitator settled the escrow.

Operator-run tooling in the controlled source checkout:

```
node scripts/check-custody-identity.cjs
node verifier/verify-financial-export.js \
evidence/discovery-phase6/closeout-release-export.json \
--trust=evidence/discovery-phase6/trust.json --json

```

Source access and dependencies are prerequisites; the repository is not represented as permissionlessly public. These are read-only verification commands, not public financial execution endpoints. The verifier uses explicit public trust inputs and public historical RPC reads without SAAX database credentials. It recomputes bindings, verifies actual signatures/evaluator permissions and the exact deployed-contract EIP-712 domain/type/action/nonce/issuedAt at execution time, then checks successful decoded calldata/events, historical state and token outcomes. Current evidence passes78 release checks and79 signed-refund checks. Walk through the verification boundaries (/blog/signed-discovery-to-testnet-finance).

The actual fulfilled service is a deterministic local SHA-256 self-test. All roles are operator-controlled. The refund evidence is an authenticated test nonfulfillment declaration. Signed seller evidence is independently checked, and a separate evaluator attestation binds it to the custody verdict because deployed V1 does not include an evidence hash in its verdict struct. This does not prove external service quality, external adoption or independent audit.

Funding requires test USDC and test ETH for gas. No public /fund, /release or /refund service is enabled. A local EVM with chain ID84532 is not public Base Sepolia proof. Earlier incomplete exports remain historical records, not silently upgraded evidence.

## Receipts, recovery and custody readiness

/receipt?txHash=&rail=x402 is a settlement-reference lookup, not the complete financial verifier. The latest live read returns HTTP 500 with a store-schema mismatch; this documentation release does not modify the database or claim that defect is fixed. Discovery and read-only MCP checks pass separately.

Recovery tests cover replacement-process issuance after durable acceptance and specific financial broadcast/reconciliation boundaries. The new producer journals the signed transaction hash before broadcast and reconciles by that hash; it does not prove every failure boundary or provide an unattended public recovery service. Reconcile unknown outcomes before retrying. Recovery explanation (/blog/unknown-payment-outcomes-agent-recovery).

CustodyV1 signed refunds and unsigned deadline refunds are different authorizations. Timeout refunds work only while Funded, not while Disputed. Only buyer or seller can raise a dispute. An unavailable evaluator can leave disputed funds frozen indefinitely; there is no admin, pause, upgrade or evaluator replacement. Newer custody/governance candidates remain under development/security review, not deployed versions. No mainnet escrow readiness or guaranteed refund is claimed.

## Supplier registration

The existing Router consumes ERC-8004 identity/reputation signals and ranks available suppliers. A registry entry is neither authentication of every Discovery publisher nor proof of actual service quality. See the identity standard explanation (/blog/erc-8004-agent-identity-draft-standard) and inspect current registration/endpoint requirements before relying on discovery.

## Pricing and subscriptions

Discovery preflight has no fee. Mainnet routing/payment fees are disclosed in the applicable challenge before authorization. Existing Premium subscriptions use Stripe: 14-day trial with card collected upfront, Developer $29/month, Business $199/month, Enterprise custom. Subscription email matching is an access key, not identity proof. Features apply as they ship; no SLA, compliance certification or outcome guarantee is implied. The website release does not alter billing logic.

## Risk and support

Read security (/security), disputes (/disputes), privacy (/privacy) and terms (/terms). SAAX is experimental software with component-specific maturity; production payments involve real funds. SAAX is not affiliated with Coinbase, Base or the ERC-8004 authors. Internal tests and independent verification software are not independent security review.

# SAAX Protocol — The Standard

## SAAX Protocol — Public Beta

SAAX Protocol is currently in public Beta. Immediate-payment functionality is available on Base mainnet, while escrow custody remains limited to testnet.

Independent external security review is pending. Although internal verification and reliability testing have been performed, these do not replace an independent security assessment.

Live transactions involve financial and technical risks, including potential loss of funds and irreversible blockchain transfers. Users should evaluate these risks carefully and use the platform at their own discretion.

This notice does not constitute a guarantee of reimbursement, dispute recovery, or financial protection.

Part of the SAAX system. The Protocol is the standard; the Network carries it; the Router is one commercial implementation of it.

## What SAAX Protocol Is

SAAX Protocol is a vendor-neutral standard for governed, contract-defined, outcome-verified, recoverable and auditable economic commitments between autonomous systems.

It defines how two parties — usually agents — enter into an economic commitment with each other: what was authorized, what was committed, what proves fulfillment, what happens on failure, how settlement is linked, and when the commitment becomes final.

SAAX is not a payment rail. It is not an identity system. It is not a marketplace. It is a standard for what a commitment means — for what must be true for a commitment to be valid, fulfilled, and final.

## Why It Exists

Autonomous agents are starting to transact with each other: buying compute, data, security services, and tools. But there is no common way for one agent to know what another agent has actually committed to — or whether it delivered.

SAAX answers the basic questions of agent commerce:

- Authority — was this actor actually authorized to make this commitment?

- Terms — what was promised, at what price, under what constraints and deadlines?

- Acceptance criteria — what objectively counts as successful fulfillment?

- Evidence — what external, independently-verifiable proof is required?

- Outcome verification — how is evidence evaluated against the criteria?

- Recovery — what happens on failure, timeout, partial completion, or dispute?

- Settlement linkage — how does an external economic settlement relate to the commitment?

- Finality — when does the commitment conclusively reach its terminal state?

- Audit — can another party reconstruct the full history?

The Protocol does not answer who you should transact with, or how value should move. Those are separate layers.

## The Commitment Lifecycle

A SAAX commitment moves through a defined sequence:

Authority → Commitment → Contract Terms → Execution → Evidence → Verification → Fulfilled or Failed → Settlement or Recovery → Finality → Audit

- Authority — proof that an autonomous actor was authorized to enter the commitment (external authority proofs are referenced, not issued by SAAX).

- Commitment — the commitment is issued with its terms, acceptance criteria, and verification policies.

- Contract Terms — what was promised, at what price, under what constraints and deadlines.

- Execution — the parties perform their obligations.

- Evidence — external, independently-verifiable proof is submitted, bound to a specific acceptance criterion.

- Verification — SAAX validates the evidence (structure, signature, provenance, binding) and evaluates it against the criterion's verification policy.

- Fulfilled or Failed — the outcome is recorded: satisfied, not satisfied, or insufficient evidence.

- Settlement or Recovery — a satisfied commitment links to settlement; a failed or partial one enters recovery semantics.

- Finality — the commitment conclusively reaches its terminal state.

- Audit — the full history can be reconstructed by another party.

## Evidence and Authority — External by Design

Two design choices separate SAAX from systems that trust the parties to declare fulfillment.

### Evidence

SAAX does not trust the buyer or seller to declare fulfillment. Evidence comes from external sources with independent verification — temperature sensors, delivery trackers, reputation oracles, inspectors, or any issuer that signs a verifiable claim.

Each evidence record binds to a commitment and a specific acceptance criterion, and is validated against:

- Structure and signature (EIP-712, COSE, or JWS schemes)

- Provenance and issuance time (freshness windows)

- Binding to the commitment and criterion

- The criterion's verification policy — required evidence type, optional accepted-issuer allowlist, evaluation logic, maximum evidence age, and minimum evidence count

### Authority

SAAX does not issue authority proofs. It consumes them from external systems — AP2 mandates, verifiable intents, OAuth tokens, or custom schemes.

Each authority proof references who issued it, who is authorized, what scope of action is authorized, and a validity window. At issuance, the commitment references the proof; at execution time, the proof is re-evaluated — still valid? still in scope?

In the current v3 agreement format, the agreement is signed directly by the parties — the buyer and the seller — and those signatures are part of the digest that is hashed and anchored. Authority proofs from external systems are an additional authorization mechanism that can be referenced by a commitment; they are not required for an agreement to be valid. The signed-agreement path is the normal path today, not a legacy fallback.

## Settlement Linkage — Rail-Neutral

SAAX does not prescribe a settlement rail.

A commitment issues a settlement requirement (R) — the amount, currency, payee, and expectation — that carries no rail knowledge. The actual rail (S) is resolved at execution time from a registered registry. The commitment knows that value will move and how much; it does not know or care which mechanism moves it.

Any system that implements the rail interface — realise a requirement into a credential, validate a credential against the requirement, settle a credential into a transaction reference — can register as a SAAX settlement rail. Currently registered rails include x402; the MPP rail is implemented but not registered in the production deployment (x402-only mode). Future rails (entitlement, card, ACH, internal ledger) can be added by implementing the same interface.

## The Network

The SAAX Network is the intended federated collection of independently operated endpoints that exchange conforming SAAX commitment messages. This is the protocol's design target — it has not yet been demonstrated with independent operators. Today the only running endpoint is the SAAX Router, operated by the SAAX team.

Any conforming node would be able to participate in the Network regardless of its underlying infrastructure, settlement rail, or commercial operator. The Network is not owned by any single party — it is the transport for commitments that conform to the Protocol. That federation is planned, not yet deployed.

## Reference Implementation

The SAAX Router is one implementation of the Protocol — an optional commercial service for discovering, ranking and matching providers and connecting commitments to supported settlement rails.

The Router currently settles on Base mainnet via USDC through x402. That is the Router's current settlement profile — a choice, not a requirement of the Protocol. The Router is the practical way to use SAAX today: integration guide (/docs), settlement endpoint (https://settlement.saax-protocol.com), MCP server (https://www.saax-protocol.com/mcp).

Other implementations are free to build on the Protocol. The Protocol does not depend on the Router; the Router depends on the Protocol.

## Implemented Discovery and the testnet financial profile

Public beta Discovery interfaces now serve a signed provider profile, free nonbinding preflight and configured-buyer acceptance creating one authenticated commitment. They do not execute payments or services. Provider identity uses independently authenticated configured-key onboarding; a profile's own public key is not an independent trust anchor.

The new connected financial demonstration uses a separately signed Base Sepolia profile and an explicit buyer-authorized financial agreement. A provider proposal signature, buyer acceptance, payment/funding authorization and evaluator verdict are different authorities. The exact selected network, asset, integer amount/decimals, mode, parties, evaluator permissions and custody remain bound throughout. A later rail or asset choice cannot override an already signed selection; it needs fresh authorization. The general rail-neutral model does not weaken a profile that explicitly selects financial terms.

This testnet preview uses actual CustodyV1 funding/release/refund with independent verification of complete signed records and public-chain facts. Its evidence is an operator-controlled deterministic SHA256 self-test, not an external service or independent audit. It does not claim the self-test uses external attesters or an EAS anchor. Mainnet immediate payments remain a separate public-beta direct-payment lane; mainnet escrow is unavailable. Integration guide (/docs), verification walkthrough (/blog/signed-discovery-to-testnet-finance), current status (/status).

## The Full Specification

Read the complete commitment lifecycle specification — evidence abstraction, authority interface, verification policies, recovery semantics, settlement-rail neutrality, and the rail interface — at the Commitment Lifecycle Spec (/spec).

SAAX components vary in maturity: the specification is public and versioned, routing and immediate payments are public beta on Base mainnet, commitment verification and receipts are beta, escrow custody is testnet preview (not approved for mainnet funds), and unreleased custody/governance candidates are under development / security review. See the current status (/status) page for details. Read the full terms of use (/terms) before using it with real funds.

Source: https://saax-protocol.com/spec

# SAAX Protocol — Commitment Lifecycle Specification

Public specification — versioned (protocol v1.0.3). This document describes the standard, not any particular implementation. Components vary in maturity: routing and immediate payments are public beta on Base mainnet, commitment verification and receipts are beta, escrow custody is testnet preview (not approved for mainnet funds), and unreleased custody/governance candidates are under development / security review. Read the full terms of use (/terms) before using it with real funds.

## 1. The Commitment Lifecycle

The SAAX commitment lifecycle is a governed commitment that moves through a defined sequence:

Authority → Commitment → Contract Terms → Execution → Evidence → Verification → Fulfilled or Failed → Settlement or Recovery → Finality → Audit

The commitment binds the terms — capability, price, acceptance criteria, deadline, cancel condition — before value moves. It carries no rail, no credential, no settlement reference: settlement is resolved at execution time.

The commitment is issued before value moves. A spend bound to a commitment must be denied if the requested amount or currency differs.

## 2. Evidence / Attestation Abstraction

### 2.1 Principle

SAAX does not trust the buyer or seller to declare fulfillment. Evidence comes from external sources with independent verification — temperature sensors, delivery trackers, reputation oracles, inspectors. SAAX validates evidence (structure, signature, provenance, binding) and evaluates it against the commitment's acceptance-criterion verification policies. SAAX never produces the evidence.

### 2.2 Evidence record schema

```
{
"evidenceId": "0x...",
"evidenceType": "temperature-reading",
"issuer": "0x...",
"subject": "0x...",
"issuanceTimestamp": "2026-10-06T...",
"contextReference": "0x...",
"payload": { ... },
"payloadHash": "sha256:...",
"provenance": { ... },
"signature": "COSE_Sign1...",
"verificationScheme": "eip712|cose|jws",
"verificationMaterial": "0x...",
"commitmentId": "0x...",
"acceptanceCriterionId": "0x..."
}

```

Every field is validated; only recognized fields are kept. The payload hash is the SHA-256 of the canonical JSON encoding of the payload — any payload tampering changes the hash and fails validation.

### 2.3 Verification-policy model

The commitment specifies a verification policy per acceptance criterion:

```
{
"criterionId": "0x...",
"criterionDescription": "delivery temperature
- Validate evidence — checks structure, signature, provenance, and binding to the commitment and criterion. A hash-vs-payload mismatch (tampering) fails validation.

- Evaluate criterion — applies the verification policy (type, allowlist, freshness, evaluation logic, minimum count) and returns satisfied | not_satisfied | insufficient_evidence.

- Record outcome — writes the result to the commitment record, bound to the commitment and criterion.

### 2.5 Evidence lifecycle

```
commitment issued
->
acceptance criteria defined with verification policies
->
external evidence submitted (from any source)
->
SAAX validates evidence (structure, signature, provenance, binding)
->
SAAX evaluates against criterion
->
outcome recorded: satisfied | not_satisfied | insufficient_evidence
->
commitment reaches finality or enters recovery

```

The signature scheme eip712 is verified cryptographically over the EIP-712 domain { name: 'SAAX Evidence', version: '1' }. cose and jws envelopes are validated structurally — envelope shape, required headers, and field typing — by the reference implementation; cryptographic verification of the token's signature requires the pluggable verifier hook to be connected to an attesting verifier (for example an issuer's public-key store). Structural validation alone does not prove who signed the token. A commitment that accepts cose/jws evidence should specify the verifier that attests it.

## 3. Authority-Proof Interface

### 3.1 Principle

A commitment references an external authority proof — AP2 mandates, verifiable intents, OAuth tokens, or custom schemes. SAAX does not issue authority proofs; it consumes them from external systems and re-evaluates them at execution time.

### 3.2 AuthorityProof structure

```
{
"authorityProofId": "0x...",
"proofType": "ap2-mandate|verifiable-intent|oauth-token|custom",
"issuer": "0x...",
"subject": "0x...",
"scope": { ... },
"validFrom": "2026-10-06T...",
"validUntil": "2026-10-07T...",
"signature": "COSE_Sign1...",
"verificationScheme": "cose|jws|eip712",
"verificationMaterial": "0x..."
}

```

Scope model: actions[] (the requested action must be in this list), optional capability, optional amountMax (raw units), optional currency. An absent scope dimension is unrestricted; a present dimension must be satisfied by the commitment.

### 3.3 Validation

- Validate authority proof — checks structure, signature, scope, and time validity.

- Is authorized — verifies the proof covers the specific action the commitment represents (combines integrity + time + scope).

- Attach to commitment — attaches the proof reference to the commitment at issuance. The full proof and its signature are never stored on the commitment — only the verifiable reference; the proof material lives at the external issuer.

### 3.4 Authority lifecycle

```
authority proof presented (external source)
->
SAAX validates proof (structure, signature, scope, time)
->
commitment issued, referencing the authority proof
->
proof evaluated at execution time (still valid? still in scope?)
->
commitment validly authorized or rejected

```

In the current v3 agreement format, an agreement without an external authority proof is signed directly by the parties — the buyer and the seller — and those signatures are part of the digest that is hashed and anchored. That is the normal path today, not a legacy fallback; external authority proofs are an additional authorization mechanism a commitment can reference.

## 4. Settlement-Rail Neutrality

SAAX does not prescribe a settlement rail.

- The commitment issues a settlement requirement (R) that is rail-agnostic: R = — no rail knowledge at commitment time.

- The rail (S) is resolved at execution time from the registered registry.

- Currently registered rails: x402. The MPP rail is implemented but not registered in production (x402-only mode).

- Future rails: entitlement, card, ACH, internal ledger — any implementation of the rail interface can register as a SAAX settlement rail.

### 4.1 Rail interface

```
interface SettlementRail {
realise(R): Credential // turn a neutral requirement into a credential
validate(Credential, R): boolean // is this credential valid FOR R?
settle(Credential): TransactionReference // move value; return PUBLIC tx reference
}

```

Any system that implements this interface can register as a SAAX settlement rail:

```
registry.register('new-rail', { realise, validate, settle });
const rail = registry.resolve('new-rail');

```

The rail knows nothing about the commitment's content; it only knows how to realise R. Rail credentials never appear in receipts, logs, or results — only the public transaction reference.

## SAAX components vary in maturity: the specification is public and versioned, routing and immediate payments are public beta on Base mainnet, commitment verification and receipts are beta, escrow custody is testnet preview (not approved for mainnet funds), and unreleased custody/governance candidates are under development / security review. Read the full terms of use. Nothing in this specification constitutes financial, legal, or investment advice.

## 5. Escrow Custody (Day 17)

SAAX escrow protects funds pending an outcome. The escrow is a separate on-chain custody contract — never an in-memory flag, never a direct transfer labelled "escrow".

Status note: the custody implementation described below refers to the hosted testnet escrow flow (Base Sepolia, chain 84532). A newer custody candidate, SAAXEscrowCustodyV3.sol, has been tested only on a local EVM (chain 31337) and is under independent-review preparation; it is not deployed and does not power any hosted flow. See current status (/status).

### 5.1 Where funds are held

Settled USDC is moved into SAAXEscrowCustodyV1 on the configured network (Base Sepolia for testnet). The contract's balanceOf(this) is the authoritative held amount — verifiable on-chain by anyone, without SAAX's database.

### 5.2 Who can release / refund / withdraw

- release(commitmentId, digest, nonce, issuedAt, v, r, s) — releases USDC to the seller. Requires an EIP-712 verdict signed by the agreed EVALUATOR (from the commitment terms, bound at fund time). msg.sender may be a relayer; the recovered signer must equal the evaluator. Wrong signer / wrong digest / expired / replayed verdict → revert.

- refund(...) — returns USDC to the buyer. Requires an evaluator-signed refund verdict OR the deadline has passed (timeout refund, no signature needed).

- raiseDispute / resolve — only the funded buyer or seller can raise a dispute (funds freeze); only the evaluator's signed verdict naming release|refund|hold resolves it.

- NO admin, NO owner, NO upgrade, NO withdraw function. Once funded, funds move ONLY to the seller (release) or buyer (refund). The deployer cannot pull funds; SAAX's database status cannot move funds.

### 5.3 Binding

Custody is bound to:
- commitment digest (bytes32, from the EAS-anchored manifest) — every terminal action requires it; wrong digest reverts.
- buyer, seller, evaluator, asset, amount, network, deadline — frozen at fund(); terminal states are final (one release OR one refund, never both).

### 5.4 Timeout / refund / dispute / evaluator / upgrade behavior

- Timeout: after deadline, refund() without a signature succeeds (funds return to buyer). Before deadline, unsigned refund reverts.

- Dispute: raiseDispute from Funded freezes funds into Disputed; direct release/refund during dispute reverts; only resolve (evaluator verdict) moves funds.

- Evaluator unavailable: a Funded escrow can use its unsigned deadline refund after the deadline. A Disputed escrow cannot use that timeout path and can remain frozen indefinitely. No automatic resolution or operator override exists.

- Upgrade: none — the contract is immutable by design.

### 5.5 Contract addresses (testnet)

- EAS: 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000021

- SchemaRegistry: 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000020

- Base Sepolia USDC: 0x036CbD53842c5426634e7929541eC2318f3dCF7e

- SAAXEscrowCustodyV1 source: contracts/SAAXEscrowCustodyV1.sol (deployed via scripts/testnet-broadcast.js --deploy-custody)

## Discovery signature and financial-profile clarification (2026-11-06)

Discovery profile 1.0.0, acceptance-v1 and manifest-v1.1+saax-proposal-bound are distinct from protocol/package v1.0.3 and older v3 agreement exports. The live Discovery path uses actual Ed25519 JWS crypto for provider proposal/SR and onboarded-buyer acceptance. The general structural COSE/JWS evidence-hook limitation in section2.5 still applies to that separate evidence interface; it must not be generalized to claim Discovery JWS is structural-only.

The public Discovery/preflight/acceptance operations create no payment, custody or service execution. Financial terms are not spending authority. A financial profile selecting network/asset/rail/mode cannot later substitute them under the general rail-neutral abstraction; the provider must issue new terms and the buyer must accept them.

The separate discovery-financial-v2 testnet export profile binds an explicitly signed Sepolia profile, exact proposal/terms/manifest digests, configured buyer authority, evaluator address/permitted decisions, custody/runtime identity, recovery rules and evidence policy. Its independent verifier checks the deployed-contract verdict, timestamp and actual successful custody/token outcome without application DB credentials. The local SHA256 self-test evidence and separate evaluator evidence-to-verdict attestation are explicitly operator-controlled, not an external attester demonstration, EAS anchor or independent audit. Details and limitations (/blog/signed-discovery-to-testnet-finance).

## 6. Durable Persistence — Implementation Profiles

The standard requires that a commitment's authoritative state survive process restarts and be recoverable by a replacement worker. It does not prescribe one storage technology. Implementations satisfy this by profile:

- Postgres profile (the reference deployment's Docker ax_router database): escrow state lives in ax_router.escrows with atomic conditional transitions; process memory is only a cache.

- File-ledger profile (the escrow-access acceptance milestone): accepted operations, nonce consumption, and reconcile outcomes are persisted to a JSON ledger with atomic rename (data/escrow-access-ledger.json). Nonce consumption happens at durable acceptance, not at external execution; an identical retry returns the recorded result; a changed payload on the same nonce is rejected.

- Memory-only profile (the x402 idempotency cache): duplicate-request responses are held in working memory and are lost on restart. This does not affect the durable escrow record.

### 6.1 Tables

- ax_router.escrows — one row per commitment; immutable binding fields (digest, buyer, seller, evaluator, amount, asset, network, deadline) + mutable state/version + tx refs + audit chain.

- ax_router.escrow_events — ordered, hash-chained audit events (append-only, FK to escrow).

- ax_router.escrow_intents — external action intents persisted BEFORE any broadcast (idempotency-keyed, unique), reconciled AFTER with the authoritative outcome.

### 6.2 Atomic transitions

upsert_escrow is a single SQL statement that:
- rejects stale writes (STALE_VERSION — a generic upsert can never clobber newer durable state),
- rejects illegal transitions (ILLEGAL_TRANSITION — e.g. held→unfunded),
- rejects any change to a terminal state (TERMINAL_STATE — released/refunded/timed_out are final).

record_escrow_intent / update_escrow_intent enforce intent lifecycle atomically: pending→broadcast once; confirmed is terminal; duplicate idempotency keys are rejected (no double broadcast).

### 6.3 Recovery

On restart, pending_escrow_intents returns all pending/broadcast/unknown intents; the replacement worker re-queries authoritative chain/service state before retrying. Unknown outcomes remain explicitly unknown until reconciled. A missing record or an absent transaction scan is never treated as proof that a broadcast did not happen: the worker must determine the on-chain outcome by reading the chain at the identified reference, and only then record it. Demonstrations: scripts/test-escrow-durable.js (14 checks), scripts/test-worker-failure.js (11 checks, real SIGKILL).

## 7. Independent Verification (Day 17)

verifier/verify-export.js runs in a fresh process with no SAAX database access and derives every result from the export + public chain data:

- Agreement digest — recomputes sha256 of the COSE_Sign1 envelope (documented algorithm) and compares to the export.

- Party authorization — recovers the EIP-712 signer of each authorization record (secp256k1) and checks it against the agreed party; never trusts a claimed signer.

- EAS anchor — reads getAttestation(uid) via the chain RPC; checks schema UID, revocable=false, and the on-chain commitment digest.

- Journal ordering — validates the hash-linked audit chain (root=commitmentId; every entryHash matches content; timestamps monotonic).

- Escrow terminal outcome — a claimed release/refund must carry a tx reference; with an RPC, the receipt must be success. Non-terminal state = explicit unknown.

- Evidence-backed release — a released escrow must cite evidence references.

Tampering classes rejected by test: modified terms, altered/reordered/missing journal events, forged evidence, wrong anchor, substituted escrow tx refs, incomplete digest, incomplete terminal escrow. Incomplete → explicit NOT VERIFIED (incomplete/unknown), never success.

Source: https://saax-protocol.com/security

# SAAX Security

## SAAX Protocol — Public Beta

SAAX Protocol is currently in public Beta. Immediate-payment functionality is available on Base mainnet, while escrow custody remains limited to testnet.

Independent external security review is pending. Although internal verification and reliability testing have been performed, these do not replace an independent security assessment.

Live transactions involve financial and technical risks, including potential loss of funds and irreversible blockchain transfers. Users should evaluate these risks carefully and use the platform at their own discretion.

This notice does not constitute a guarantee of reimbursement, dispute recovery, or financial protection.

Last verified: 2026-11-06

SAAX is experimental software. This document describes the security posture of the SAAX Protocol and the SAAX Router, the classes of threats they are designed to defend against, and how to report a vulnerability. It distinguishes what is deployed and enforced on the live mainnet Router, what is implemented and tested in the integrated testnet escrow flow, and what remains unverified or out of scope.

## Scope

SAAX protects for four properties:

- Commitment integrity — a commitment record, once issued, cannot be silently altered; its terms, parties, evidence, and references are attributable and auditable.

- Settlement correctness — value moves only when the settlement requirement of a valid commitment is satisfied, and moves exactly as the commitment specifies.

- Reputation integrity — reputation signals derive from verifiable on-chain behavior and signatures, not self-declared claims.

- Availability of the routing layer — the routing service remains responsive to legitimate requests under load and resets cleanly after overload or operator action.

## Threat model

SAAX defends against the following attack classes. They are described generically; the precise controls are shared with operators and reviewers under coordinated disclosure.

- Duplicate charges — an attacker replays a payment authorization to extract value more than once. Mitigated by idempotency keys bound to each commitment (enforced on the live Router and in the escrow flow).

- Gas abuse and denial of service — an attacker floods the routing layer to exhaust computational or network resources. Mitigated by per-origin rate limiting.

- Nonce replay — an attacker replays a signed transfer authorization whose nonce was already consumed. Mitigated by nonce-bound idempotency: each authorization is tied to a unique nonce and settles at most once.

- Spoofed buyer reputation — an attacker fabricates a reputation signal for an address they do not control. Mitigated by deriving reputation from signatures and on-chain records rather than claimed identity.

- Signature forgery — an attacker forges an authorization or attestation. Mitigated by typed, domain-separated signature schemes (EIP-712) and contract scanning aware of proxy-upgrade patterns.

- Prompt injection via untrusted input — an attacker embeds instructions in free-text fields that a downstream system might execute. Mitigated by a sanitization gate that strips control content from untrusted input before it is processed. This is a defense-in-depth control; it does not eliminate the risk of prompt injection in any downstream model or agent.

- Supply-side fraud — a provider advertises capabilities it cannot deliver. Mitigated by a capability floor and reputation weighting that ranks providers on verified performance rather than self-declaration.

- Credential leakage — an operator's secret material is exposed to the network. Mitigated by a non-custodial design: the protocol never requires buyer funds to be held by the routing layer. Secret material is handled under a non-leakage architecture. On mainnet, the Router is non-custodial (payments are direct x402 authorizations from the buyer's wallet). In the testnet escrow flow, funds are held by the custody contract, not by the Router's operator.

## Mitigations in place — by deployment

The following table states where each control is enforced.

| Control | What it does | Where |
| Idempotency | Duplicate requests carrying the same idempotency key return the cached response and do not re-process value movement. | Live Router (mainnet immediate payments) |
| Rate limiting | Requests in excess of the per-origin window are rejected with HTTP 429. | Live Router |
| Nonce-bound settlement | Payment authorizations are bound to unique nonces; a spent nonce cannot be replayed. | Live Router; testnet escrow (per-verdict nonce consumed at acceptance) |
| Signature-derived reputation | Reputation resolves from signatures and on-chain feedback, not claimed identity or client-supplied headers. | Live Router (reads ERC-8004 identity registry) |
| Typed verification | Authorizations use typed, domain-separated signing (EIP-712); contract interactions are scanned with proxy-upgrade awareness. | Live Router; testnet escrow (EIP-712 verdicts/access auth) |
| Input sanitization | Untrusted fields are sanitized at the boundary; empty or malformed payloads are rejected with HTTP 422. | Live Router |
| Trusted-proxy handling | When deployed behind a reverse proxy, client addressing is read from the proxy-provided header so rate limits cannot be bypassed by proxy rotation. | Live Router (deployment-specific) |
| Kill switch | An operator-controlled halt returns HTTP 503 before any value movement or external call. | Live Router |
| Escrow chain guard | Every transaction-capable path refuses a chain other than Base Sepolia (84532) for escrow flows; mainnet escrow custody is never enabled. | Testnet escrow instance only |
| Durable acceptance ledger | Accepted operations, nonce consumption, and reconcile outcomes are persisted durably (JSON ledger with atomic rename) so a replacement worker can reconcile without re-executing. | Testnet escrow instance (durable file); Postgres profile in the reference deployment |
| EAS anchoring | Agreements are anchored via EAS attestation on-chain for independent verification. | Testnet escrow flow (live EAS on Base Sepolia) |

## Discovery and financial verification boundaries

Public signed Discovery, free preflight and configured-buyer acceptance are deployed beta interfaces. They verify real Ed25519 JWS signatures for their defined records and persist a single authenticated commitment, but do not fund, pay, execute a service or release custody. Provider identity requires an independently installed configured key; a self-declared key is not permissionless authentication. Buyer public keys are separately onboarded and scoped.

The isolated financial preview requires a separately signed Base Sepolia profile and exact network/CAIP-19 asset agreement through proposal, buyer acceptance, commitment and execution. A mainnet-bound proposal cannot become testnet authorization because an environment variable or RPC endpoint changed. The production mainnet profile and immediate-payment behavior remain separate and unchanged.

The exact deployed CustodyV1 runtime, committed artifact and pinned-source compilation match in full:6934 runtime bytes =6881 executable +51 CBOR metadata +2 length bytes, compiled with solc 0.8.26, optimizer 200, viaIR, Cancun. The earlier guessed metadata trim was incorrect. Identity is not proof of safety or independent review.

The expanded separate-process financial verifier authenticates configured provider and buyer keys, complete terms/digests/versions and evaluator permissions, then checks the actual deployed EIP-712 domain/type/action/nonce/issuedAt at execution-block time, successful decoded transaction calldata/events, historical escrow state, token transfers and balances. Signed seller evidence is checked against its policy; a separate evaluator signature connects its digest to the custody verdict. V1 does not directly include an evidence hash in its verdict struct.

This result applies to a deterministic local SHA256 self-test with real Base Sepolia custody, not independently observed external service quality. All test roles are operator-controlled. Historical exports lacking the signed profile/evaluator/evidence chain remain explicitly incomplete; valid old transactions are preserved. General COSE/JWS authority/evidence hooks elsewhere retain their format-specific structural/attesting-verifier limitations. No blanket cryptographic-verification or audit claim follows.

## Residual risks

SAAX does not fully eliminate the following risks, and users should assume they exist:

- Smart contract risk — the settlement contracts and the tokens they move may contain undiscovered defects; on-chain behavior is final.

- Key compromise at the user layer — if a participant's own keys are compromised, no protocol control can prevent loss.

- Censorship and liveness — routing availability depends on the operators of the routing node and on the Base network; neither SAAX nor any user can force either to remain available.

- RPC dependence — settlement correctness depends on the RPC providers serving on-chain data; a malicious or degraded provider can delay or distort observed state.

- Reputation gaming — colluding parties can manipulate on-path reputation over time; reputation weighting reduces but does not eliminate this.

- Social engineering — operators and integrators can be induced to misconfigure deployments; no technical control fully prevents operator error.

- Evaluator dependence (escrow) — in the escrow flow, disputed funds can be released or refunded only by the evaluator whose address is bound in the agreement. If that evaluator disappears, the disputed escrow cannot be resolved by anyone else. This is a design property of the testnet custody contract, not a bug.

- Recovery boundaries — replacement-process Discovery issuance and specific financial broadcast/reconciliation scenarios have test evidence. The new isolated producer persists its signed transaction hash before broadcast; this does not prove every older driver, failure boundary, external provider or unattended deployment recovers. Recovery remains explicit and operator-assisted, not a universal guarantee.

- Prompt injection — input sanitization reduces but cannot eliminate prompt-injection risk in downstream models, agents, or tools.

## Audit status

SAAX has no independent security audit of the protocol implementation, the Router, or the testnet custody contract as of this update. Passing conformance vectors and internal test suites are not an audit and do not constitute a security certification. The custody contract is testnet-only research code; it has not been reviewed by an independent custodian or auditor, and it is not production custody.

Custody V3 candidate: a newer custody candidate (SAAXEscrowCustodyV3.sol) has been tested only on a local EVM (chain 31337) with synthetic keys. An independent-review snapshot package has been prepared and owner-approved as the baseline for independent review; no independent security review has been completed — the project owner is seeking a suitable review firm, and no engagement or endorsement is implied. Approval-for-review is not an audit, not production readiness, and not deployment approval. Local test counts and local anchors are not independent security assurance or public-chain finality. See current status (/status).

## Non-custodial claim, scoped

On mainnet, the Router is non-custodial: immediate x402 payments move directly from the buyer's wallet to the payee; the Router never holds buyer funds. In the testnet escrow flow, funds are held by the SAAXEscrowCustodyV1 contract — that is custody by a smart contract, not by the operator — and it is testnet-only. "Non-custodial" does not mean "no funds are ever held anywhere": it means the routing operator does not hold them. The Custody V3 candidate is local only and is not part of any hosted flow.

## Out of scope

SAAX is not designed to protect against:

- Compromise of a user's own private keys or wallet software.

- Malicious behavior of counterparties outside the commitment's terms (e.g., off-protocol fraud, delivery of defective goods despite passing acceptance criteria).

- Financial loss from market movement, token volatility, or failed external systems.

- Legal or regulatory consequences of using the protocol in a given jurisdiction.

- Attacks on the underlying networks (Base), the USDC contract, or the RPC infrastructure SAAX depends on.

- Losses arising from user error, including sending funds to the wrong address or misreading commitment terms.

## Reporting a vulnerability

If you believe you have found a security issue in SAAX, please report it by email:

To report a security concern, email reachsaaxprotocol@gmail.com.

Please include:

- A description of the vulnerability and its impact.

- The component affected (protocol, routing service, contracts, or docs).

- Steps to reproduce, including any payloads or request sequences.

- Your contact details if you would like a reply.

What we commit to:

- Acknowledgment within five business days of receipt.

- Triage and a first response within ten business days.

- Coordinated disclosure — we will work with you on a disclosure timeline (typically up to 90 days) before public discussion, unless the issue is already public or being actively exploited.

Do not test against production accounts, live funds, or the mainnet settlement contracts beyond what is necessary to demonstrate an issue. Use small amounts. Reports are handled on a best-effort, non-guaranteed timeline; this is experimental software maintained by a small team.

— SAAX Protocol

Source: https://saax-protocol.com/disputes

# SAAX Disputes

Last updated: 2026-10-06

SAAX standardizes recovery and dispute states within the commitment lifecycle. It does not guarantee reimbursement, reversal, or resolution of disputes. This page explains when to open a dispute or complaint, how to file one, what happens next, and what SAAX can and cannot do.

## When to use this channel

A dispute or complaint is appropriate when:

- A commitment you participated in did not behave as its terms stated (for example, settlement moved the wrong amount, or a state transition contradicted the recorded terms).

- You believe a settled commitment was charged incorrectly or duplicated.

- You believe the routing service misbehaved — a failure to respond, an incorrect error, or an availability problem that caused you loss.

- You believe someone is misusing the SAAX name or the protocol to defraud users.

- You have a privacy or data-handling concern (those can also go to the privacy contact).

This channel is not for:

- Disagreements with a counterparty about the quality of goods or services that fell outside the commitment's acceptance criteria. SAAX does not arbitrate commerce; it records terms and outcomes.

- Market losses, volatility, or losses from your own key management.

- Anything already resolved on-chain that you simply want reversed — on-chain records are immutable and cannot be undone.

## How to file

Email the dispute team at:

For dispute inquiries, email reachsaaxprotocol@gmail.com.

Please include:

- Commitment ID — the commitment identifier from the request or the 402 challenge (if you have one).

- Description of the issue — what happened, when, and what you expected instead.

- Evidence — transaction hashes, request/response payloads, timestamps, screenshots, or any other material that supports your account.

- Your wallet address(es) — so we can correlate records (remember: on-chain records are public).

- Contact details — where you want a reply.

The more evidence you include, the faster we can investigate. Requests with no commitment ID or evidence may be returned for more information.

## Expected response time

Best-effort, non-guaranteed. SAAX components vary in maturity — immediate payments are public beta on Base mainnet, escrow custody is testnet-only preview (not approved for mainnet funds), and custody/governance candidates are under development / security review. This service is maintained by a small team. We aim to:

- Acknowledge receipt within five business days.

- Provide an initial response (status or next step) within ten business days.

These are targets, not commitments. Complex investigations — especially those requiring on-chain analysis or correlation across providers — can take longer. We will not claim a response-time SLA.

## Resolution process

After a dispute is filed:

- Acknowledgment — you receive confirmation of receipt and a reference.

- Triage — we classify the issue (commitment misbehavior, service failure, process error, or misuse) and assign it.

- Investigation — we review the commitment record, the relevant transactions, and any evidence you provided, consulting public on-chain data and provider records where needed.

- Findings — we tell you what the records show: what happened, whether the protocol behaved per its terms, and whether an operator error occurred.

- Outcome — where the operator is at fault (for example, a service misconfiguration that caused loss), we will state what we can do: a correction of private records, an explanation, or — only where feasible and within the protocol's capabilities — a good-faith accommodation. Where the protocol behaved per its terms, the finding is that the commitment stands as recorded.

- Closure — the dispute is closed with a written summary. Closing a dispute does not alter immutables: on-chain transactions are not reversed by a dispute outcome.

## Escalation

If the initial response does not resolve the issue:

- Reply to the same thread asking for escalation, and we will route it to a senior operator.

- Re-file with additional evidence if you believe something was missed.

- If the issue involves an external party — the token contract (USDC), the Base network, or a hosting provider — we will tell you how to escalate to them, since those are outside SAAX's control.

There is no formal appeals body beyond the operators. Independent arbitration is possible only if the parties agree to it in the commitment's terms; SAAX does not provide arbitration.

## How disputes actually resolve (escrow flow)

In the integrated escrow flow (Base Sepolia testnet), a dispute is a real on-chain state: only the funded buyer or seller can call the custody contract to raise a dispute, which freezes the funds. From that point the funds can move only by an evaluator-signed verdict under the deployed contract's rules — release or refund (recorded as resolve:release / resolve:refund). There is no operator override, no admin withdrawal, and no automatic timer that resolves a dispute.

This means disputes are evaluator-dependent: the evaluator address bound in the agreement is the only entity that can resolve a disputed escrow. If the evaluator does not act — or disappears — the disputed funds remain locked indefinitely. Only buyer or seller can initiate it; only the evaluator's signed verdict can resolve it. The timeout-refund path does not run while an escrow is disputed.

This limitation is a design property of the testnet custody contract, and it applies to the testnet research flow only. Mainnet immediate payments have no dispute state at all: settlement is final.

## Support vs. on-chain disputes

Contacting support (reachsaaxprotocol@gmail.com) is a complaint channel, not an on-chain action. It will not freeze funds, move funds, or start an on-chain dispute. On-chain dispute initiation is performed against the custody contract by a participant, and resolution requires the evaluator's signed verdict as described above. A support complaint and an on-chain dispute are separate processes; neither guarantees a refund or a favorable outcome.

## What SAAX can and cannot do

SAAX standardizes recovery and dispute states within the commitment lifecycle. It does not guarantee reimbursement, reversal, or resolution of disputes. Enforcement depends on the parties involved and any arbitration mechanisms they agree to.

Specifically:

- We can: investigate, explain what the records show, correct private working-memory records, and (where operator error caused loss) make a good-faith accommodation within the protocol's capabilities.

- We cannot: reverse on-chain transactions, edit immutable records, force a counterparty to pay, guarantee a favorable outcome, or make you whole for market or counterparty losses.

## Contact

- Disputes: reachsaaxprotocol@gmail.com

- Privacy: reachsaaxprotocol@gmail.com

- Security: reachsaaxprotocol@gmail.com

— SAAX Protocol

# SAAX Protocol — Essays
```
